subject: Life Skills
title: The Pomodoro Technique
description: A quick win: understand The Pomodoro Technique.

hook.text: A university student in the 1980s used a tomato-shaped kitchen timer and accidentally invented a global method.

buildup.text: Francesco Cirillo set his timer for 25 minutes, worked without interruption, then took a 5-minute break. Repeat.

discovery.text: The magic is the constraint. Knowing the timer will ring in 25 minutes makes starting feel low-risk and doable.

twist.text: The break is not optional. Skipping it leads to burnout by lunch. Your brain consolidates learning during rest.

climax.text: After four pomodoros, take a longer 15–30 minute break. This rhythm matches your brain's ultradian cycles.

punchline.text: 25 minutes on, 5 off. Tiny sprints win the race.

quiz.question: Why does the Pomodoro Technique reduce procrastination?
options: 25 minutes feels like a small commitment, making starting easier
The tomato timer creates a sense of urgency
It eliminates the need for breaks
